recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not edit MedicationRequest for FHIR-26595 unless the work group wants to revisit the later FHIR-39119 resource-guidance wording; handle FHIR-54095 separately if Resolved - change required technical corrections are in scope.
issue_request: FHIR-26595 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification R5 Pharmacy change request asking the MedicationRequest Scope and Usage and boundaries guidance to clarify when MedicationRequest is appropriate for products involving medication. The approved text allowed medication-related devices such as prefilled PCA, insulin, or narcotic syringes and clarified that medication-coated devices such as heparin-coated stents are not MedicationRequest orders.
initial_application: The issue appears to have been applied by d61b35bbd4e574c019f315e930d78e4341cde26a on 2022-01-21. That commit's subject includes FHIR-26595 and its patch added the prefilled-syringe examples and medication-coated-device exclusion to source/medicationrequest/medicationrequest-introduction.xml.
additional_context: MedicationRequest is active approved build-scope source in source/fhir.ini. The current Scope and Usage text still includes the seed examples and exclusion. A later Published issue, FHIR-39119, intentionally replaced the original OR/material-management wording with Device Request/SupplyRequest resource guidance and is already represented on the combined branch. FHIR-54095 is a later Resolved - change required typo request for the same paragraph and was not decided in this Applied/Published run.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. No source change is needed because the current active MedicationRequest narrative already conveys the seed's substantive rule, while restoring the original OR/material-management sentence would conflict with later accepted FHIR-39119 wording.
